h: The Sons of Yosef and the Limits of Temporary Rulings

p: at the end of this book,
which is the conclusion of the Written Torah
and it is the beginning of
the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh
the claim of the sons of Yosef,
and it was said to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him (Bamidbar 36:5):
just as it was said of the daughters of Tzelofchad;
it is not mentioned regarding them
as with the daughters of Tzelofchad,
about whom Rashi says (Parshas Pinchas, Bamidbar 27:7)
מַה שֶּׁלֹּא רָאָה עֵינוֹ שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה
what the eye of Moshe did not see,
and "fortunate is the one born of woman
whose words HaKadosh Baruch Hu acknowledges."
that in truth it is mentioned
in the words of Chazal (end of Taanis, 30b)
that on the day the tribes were permitted
that there be love and unity
and that they intermingle with one another.
However, the sons of Yosef specifically,
because the inheritance of the land
for the need of the hour,
and for the need of the hour
And for this reason one may say
that it is stated here with the expression
as we have already spoken of this,
that Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, has
no connection at all to this matter;
and his prophecy of "zeh hadavar" means
the Shechinah speaks from within his throat
כִּי דָּבָר שֶׁהוּא רַק לְצוֹרֶךְ שָׁעָה
a matter that is only for the need of the hour
stems from the power of the enactment of the Sages,
but because the hour requires it.
with the aspect of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who is the root of the Written Torah,
it was the will of Hashem Yisbarach,
for the need of the hour,
And therefore this matter is mentioned
at the end of the Written Torah;
and also therefore it is not said here
Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him;
for that is no great thing,
has no connection to his aspect.
that HaKadosh Baruch Hu acknowledges his words,
for there was no acknowledgment here

paragraphs.text: Source: Bava Basra 121a — “אמר רב יהודה אמר שמואל: יום שהותרו שבטים לבא זה בזה. מאי דרוש? ״זה הדבר״ – דבר זה לא יהא נוהג אלא בדור זה.” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 251) — “Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says: This was the day when the members of different tribes were permitted to marry into one another’s tribe. Such marriages were restricted for the first generation to enter Eretz Yisrael, as discussed above (120a). …”

paragraphs.text: Source: Bamidbar 36:6 — “זה הדבר אשר צוה יהוה לבנות צלפחד לאמר לטוב בעיניהם תהיינה לנשים אך למשפחת מטה אביהם תהיינה לנשים” — “This is what יהוה has commanded concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: They may become the wives of anyone they wish, provided they become wives within a clan of their father’s tribe.”
